name: Street Corn Chicken Rice Bowl

ingredients.buy: 2/3 cup crumbled; 1/2 cup crumbled, for topping
juice and zest of 3 1/2 limes; 7 tablespoons
1/2 cup chopped; 2/3 cup chopped; 1 1/2 cups leaves, for topping

writer_notes: All 20 locked ingredients are used by a step; no step uses an unbought item. Water is referenced in the rice method and now stated as 7 cups, but it is uncosted and not in the locked list, so it is not treated as a shopped ingredient.

Sea Salt carries two amounts in the locked view (1 3/4 tsp and 3 1/2 tsp): the first is the chicken spice blend, the second is the rice water. Plain Salt (1 scant tsp) is the corn salad. Both prose and steps keep them distinct.

Cotija appears in two uses (2/3 cup in the salad, 1/2 cup as topping); cilantro appears in three (1/2 cup rice, 2/3 cup salad, 1 1/2 cups topping). Lime shows as Lime Juice (juice+zest of 3 1/2 limes for the salad; 7 tbsp for the rice) plus a separate Lime Zest line (3 1/2 tsp for the rice). Prose and steps reference each use without inventing or double-counting an amount.
No cost_lines were supplied in this dispatch, so shop_smart makes no per-package or per-ounce savings claims. The only money in prose is the ${{cost_ps}} token and the $1/month membership line.

Macros used only from the locked view. Per-serving stat is 45g protein (44.6 pre-rounding) and 597 cal; prose and head.description now carry the stat figure 45g rather than the pre-round 44. Band satisfied (450-800 cal, protein >= 40). No number was computed in prose.

prose.intro_html:
Mexican street corn, the kind you get on a stick from a cart with lime running down your wrist, is one of the best things a few cheap pantry spices can do. The problem is you cannot pack a paper tray of elote into a work bag and expect it to survive Tuesday. So we did the sensible thing and built it into a bowl.

This is seared chili-lime chicken over cilantro lime rice, with a cold, creamy street corn salad spooned right on top and a scatter of avocado, red onion, cilantro and cotija to finish. It hits like takeout and costs like a pantry. Fourteen containers out of one skillet and one pot of rice, and every one of them carries 45 grams of protein and stays under 600 calories. That is a full week and change of dinner handled, no drive-through required.
prose.shop_smart:
Lean on the shelf-stable stuff, because this recipe was built for it. Canned whole kernel corn is the move for the salad. You are draining it and folding it into yogurt and lime, so you gain nothing from fresh and you skip the shucking. Grab enough cans to reach seven cups drained and you are set.

Buy the chicken breast as a family pack rather than the small tray. You need four and three quarter pounds of it, and the big pack is how a bulk cook is supposed to shop. Cut it into one-inch chunks yourself at home.

The spice drawer carries this dish, so check what you already own before you add to cart: chili powder, cumin, smoked paprika, garlic powder and onion powder are the whole lineup, and most kitchens already have every one of them. That leaves the cotija, the Greek yogurt and a couple of limes as the only fresh things you are really shopping for.
prose.make_it:
Start the rice. Bring 7 cups water to a boil in a medium pot, then stir in the rice and the sea salt. Cover it, drop the heat to low, and let it simmer about 20 minutes until the rice is tender and the water is gone. While it steams, stir the chopped cilantro together with the lime juice and lime zest, then fold the warm rice through it. That is your cilantro lime base.

Mix the street corn. In a big bowl, combine the drained corn, the Greek yogurt, the cotija, the mayonnaise, the lime juice and zest, the diced jalapeno if you are using it, the cilantro and the salt. Stir it gently until it is creamy, then taste it and set it aside cold. This is the part that makes the whole bowl taste like the cart.

Season the chicken. In a small bowl, stir together the chili powder, the sea salt, the cumin, the smoked paprika, the garlic powder and the onion powder. Cut the chicken into one-inch chunks and toss them in the spice blend until every piece is coated.

Sear the chicken. Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook the chicken 4 to 5 minutes per side, until it is cooked through and reads 165F on a thermometer, working in batches so the pan is never crowded.

Build the rice base. Divide the warm cilantro lime rice among the 14 containers and spread it flat to leave room for the toppings.

Top and finish. Add the chicken, a scoop of the cold street corn salad, cubed avocado, red onion, cilantro and a last sprinkle of cotija to each bowl, then finish with a squeeze of lime.
prose.portion_html:
Here is how you make 14 even containers without guessing. Do not eyeball it. Weigh the pot of finished cilantro lime rice, subtract the empty pot, and divide what is left by 14. That gram number is your rice line in every container, and it is the difference between everybody getting fed and the last three people getting a spoonful.

The seared chicken splits the same way: weigh it, divide by 14, and lay that weight into each bowl so the protein is even across the batch. The street corn salad and the fresh toppings, the avocado, red onion, cilantro and that last dusting of cotija, go on cold at the end, either right before the lid or the morning you eat it so the avocado stays green. Portion those by eye across the 14 bowls and you are done, with every container weighing out the same.
prose.cost_closing_html:
Run the numbers and this bowl comes in at ${{cost_ps}} a serving. That is a street-cart dinner, seasoned chicken and a creamy corn salad and avocado on top, for less than the drink you would order to go with the real thing. Fourteen of them out of one shop.

The membership that gets you every recipe like this one, priced against the actual Omaha shelf, runs a dollar a month. One bowl of takeout costs more than a year of knowing exactly what your dinner costs before you cook it.
prose.upsell_html: Make it once and you will see why it earns a rotation spot: it reheats without turning sad, the cold corn salad wakes it right back up, and it never tastes like leftovers. If this is the kind of eating you want on repeat, the whole library is built the same way, real macros, real prices, no mystery. Come cook the rest of it with us.

head.description: Meal-prep street corn chicken rice bowls: chili-lime chicken over cilantro lime rice with a creamy Mexican street corn salad, avocado and cotija. 14 servings, 45g protein and under 600 calories each.

steps: Bring 7 cups water to a boil in a medium pot, then stir in the rice and sea salt. Cover, reduce the heat to low, and simmer about 20 minutes until the rice is tender and the water is absorbed. Stir the chopped cilantro with the lime juice and lime zest, then fold in the warm rice.
In a large bowl, combine the drained corn, Greek yogurt, cotija, mayonnaise, lime juice and zest, diced jalapeno if using, cilantro and salt. Stir gently until creamy, taste, and set aside cold.
In a small bowl, stir together the chili powder, sea salt, cumin, smoked paprika, garlic powder and onion powder. Toss the chicken chunks in the spice blend until fully coated.
Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook the chicken 4 to 5 minutes per side, until cooked through and it reaches 165F, working in batches if needed.
Divide the warm cilantro lime rice among the containers and spread it out to leave room for toppings.
Top each bowl with chicken, a scoop of the street corn salad, cubed avocado, red onion, cilantro, a sprinkle of cotija and a squeeze of lime.
